extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies with adjudicatory and rule‑making functions, agency counsel, and the federal judiciary
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and explanatory comments (1953) advising the President, the Judicial Conference, and federal agencies on procedural reforms to reduce unnecessary delay, expense, and voluminous records in administrative adjudication and rulemaking. The document sets forth specific rules, practices, and organizational proposals for agencies and courts to adopt or consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend creation of an Office of Administrative Procedure and that provision be made for its establishment in the Department of Justice under supervision of the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: continuous studies, cooperative efforts among agencies and the bar, collection/publication of facts and statistics, and assistance in formulation and improvement of administrative procedures. The office is advisory/research in nature and not empowered to dictate procedures; it should be headed by a Director with a small staff and use existing administrative services for economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office should (a) carry on continuous studies of adequacy of agency procedures, (b) initiate cooperative efforts to develop/adopt uniform rules of practice/procedure, (c) collect and publish facts and statistics about agency procedures, and (d) assist agencies and the Conference in formulating and improving administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be cooperative with advisory groups from agencies and the bar; analysis by statistical and other methods is expected to enable constructive suggestions. The Office should not be given coercive power over agencies and should commence studies without regard to unresolved issues about hearing examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office structure and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office should consist of a Director and a staff; the Director to be appointed for an indefinite term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation envisions a small research/advisory organization headed by a single Director (not a board). Location in DOJ recommended for legal focus and economical use of existing services; Director should secure advice from agency/bar representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's advisory arrangements and agency cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director should make arrangements to secure advice of representatives of agencies, the bar and other interested persons; each agency should promptly furnish information requested by the Director and assist him by appropriate means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on mutual cooperation; Office effectiveness depends on agency support and ready access to up-to-date factual information about agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage exclusion of irrelevant/immaterial/repetitious evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge United States Courts to encourage hearing officers and agencies in formal administrative proceedings to exclude irrelevant, immaterial and repetitious evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commentary notes excessive leniency in admitting marginal evidence is often driven by prior judicial criticism; courts should occasionally commend proper exclusions to counteract habits of over-admission that increase delay, expense and record volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform rules on certification and filing of record on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a uniform rule in Courts of Appeals providing (a) time for filing certified record, (b) that record may be shortened/abbreviated to include only parts necessary to decide issues (by stipulation or court order), and (c) that supplemental records may be certified (by stipulation or court order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective: avoid burdens of certifying voluminous unnecessary records. Use is permissive with parties' stipulation or court discretion; some statutes permit abbreviated records while others preclude them, so legislative amendments may be needed for universal application. Courts and agencies have adopted similar rules in many circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing briefs prior to printing of full record (joint printed appendix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a uniform rule allowing, by stipulation or court order, filing of a joint printed appendix containing record matters relied on by the parties after briefs are written (with binding effect when stipulated or ordered), with responsibilities and timing specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key mechanics: petitioner generally responsible for printing appendix but not for other parties' failures; joint appendix must be indexed/paged for ready reference; prescribed timing: petitioner's brief within 40 days after transcript filed, respondent's brief within 30 days after petitioner's, petitioner's reply within 15 days of respondent's, joint printed appendix not later than 10 days prior to oral argument. Procedure designed to reduce printing of unnecessary parts of the record and save cost/volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider unnecessary delay, expense and record volume detrimental
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency should consider unnecessary delay, expense, and volume of records in adjudicatory and rule-making proceedings to be detrimental to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the underlying philosophy: focus on eliminating only unnecessary burdens while preserving justice; promotes efficiency and public interest over complacent tolerance of protracted proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive study of agency procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency having adjudicatory or rule-making functions should make a comprehensive and intensive study of its own procedures to discover and eliminate unnecessary delay, expense, or volume of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are responsible for examining their particular types of proceedings and tailoring reforms to their functions and circumstances; combined exchange of information among agencies is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define status and authority of agency counsel by rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should define by rule the status of agency counsel including: (a) authority to participate, (b) whether participation is mandatory or permissive, (c) when counsel must be served with notices/papers, (d) whether counsel is an advocate or limited to development of relevant materials, (e) authority to stipulate facts/testimony, and (f) authority to settle controversies or transmit settlement offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear rules about counsel status avoid wasted hearing time spent proving undisputed matters and clarify when counsel may make stipulations or settlements; tailored rules will assist agency counsel and private bar in practice before agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require precise definition of issues before hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should require that issues to be adjudicated be made as precise as possible initially so hearing officers proceed promptly on relevant material only; require particularity in complaints, answers, applications for rules/licenses, and petitions to intervene; single-party hearings should have orders specifying issues to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharper issues reduce time, expense, and cluttered records. The document warns against in camera selection of issues and recommends issue sharpening first by papers of record and then in prehearing conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage prehearing and intra-hearing conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should encourage hearing officers to call and conduct prehearing conferences and other conferences during hearings to simplify, clarify and dispose of issues and shorten proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prehearing conferences (round-table meetings) help cull uncontested issues, formulate efficient hearing plans (order of proof, written vs oral testimony), promote stipulations, and reduce record volume; but they require thorough preparation and exchange of supporting documents beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt formal prehearing conference rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should adopt a prehearing conference rule (or similar) authorizing the agency or hearing officer to direct parties to appear for a conference to consider (a) simplification of issues, (b) necessity of amendments to pleadings, (c) obtaining stipulations/admissions, (d) limitation on number of expert witnesses, and (e) other matters aiding disposition; the officer shall make an order reciting actions taken and limiting issues to those not disposed of, which controls subsequent proceedings unless modified for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled after Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16; attendance mandatory, order is binding unless later modified for good cause, and the rule authorizes summary disposition if parties willfully disregard conference notices. The rule aims to curtail protracted hearings by producing enforceable prehearing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require advance submission of documentary evidence where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should require, where practicable, that all documentary evidence to be offered during taking of evidence be submitted to the hearing examiner and other parties sufficiently in advance for study and preparation; evidence not submitted may be excluded absent good cause; authenticity of documents submitted in advance deemed admitted unless timely written objection filed (subject to good cause to challenge later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to reduce quantity of material, allow focused cross-examination and rebuttal, shorten hearing time and transcript size, and produce better organized records. 'Documentary evidence' includes written exhibits and any required written testimony. 'Good cause' exceptions include unforeseeable needs such as impeachment material; hearing examiner discretion governs sanctions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require prepared excerpts of documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When only portions of a document are relied upon, the offering party shall prepare and supply to the hearing examiner and other parties pertinent excerpts, identified and accompanied by a statement of purpose; only those excerpts shall be received into the record, with the whole original made available for examination/use by opposing counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the practice of offering entire documents for incorporation by reference, forces counsel to identify relevant portions in advance, shortens records, and facilitates examination in judicial review. Opposing counsel may prepare additional excerpts for cross-examination as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require agency counsel to prepare trial briefs in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should require agency counsel to prepare adequate detailed trial briefs in appropriate cases in advance of hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance trial briefs help ensure thorough preparation, reduce dilatory tactics, and result in shorter, better organized hearings and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant hearing officers broad authority on interlocutory matters and minimize interlocutory appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should grant hearing officers broad authority to rule on interlocutory matters arising during hearings and should reduce interlocutory appeals to a minimum; interlocutory appeals that are permitted should be disposed of promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation provides timely rulings from the officer 'living with the case' and reduces delays caused by liberal interlocutory appeal practices that undermine officers' authority. For significant matters, agencies should create expedited machinery (example: FTC Motions Commissioner practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index long records (indexing practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any formal proceeding where the record will exceed 2,500 pages, provide by counsel or agency staff a daily/current index of the record available to the hearing officer and all counsel; the index should be topical (not a digest) and as a minimum identify topics, witnesses testifying on each topic, pages where testimony appears, and exhibit numbers; include separate cards for each witness and topics on which they testified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current topical index permits orderly presentation, prompt preparation of findings, quicker counsel argument preparation, and reduced time needed to study the record. Cites experience from long cases demonstrating clear efficiency gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an adequate Attorneys' Manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should maintain an adequate and detailed attorneys' manual for guidance of agency counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuals provide consistent internal guidance to agency counsel, supporting thorough preparation and uniform practice before the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish in-service training for agency counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should establish in-service training for agency counsel, including systematic regular instruction for newly-hired attorneys over a definite period and periodic refresher courses or 'trial clinics' for experienced attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training promotes better prepared counsel, reduces dilatory tactics, and enhances the quality and efficiency of hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish practice manuals for practitioners before agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should publish advisory practice manuals detailing procedural steps for each type of proceeding under statutes the agency administers, together with customary forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice manuals make expectations transparent for outside practitioners, reduce procedural confusion, and encourage efficient case preparation and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate in lawyers' institutes and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should cooperate with universities and bar associations in conducting practicing lawyers' institutes or specialized courses in administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation supports practitioner education, improves practice quality before agencies, and fosters better mutual understanding between agencies and the bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor conferences with the agency bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should sponsor informal local, regional or national meetings between responsible officials and members of the agency bar to foster understanding and cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conferences are good public relations, help create cooperative atmospheres, and can lead to practical improvements in procedures and reduced litigation inefficiencies.
